parsed.summary: For a finite nonempty IFS φ_i(x) = r_i x + t_i on ℝ with 0 < |r_i| < 1 and strictly positive probability weights p_i, the theorem states the following. Any probability measure μ satisfying μ = Σ p_i (φ_i)_*μ has lower Hausdorff dimension (inf of dim_H E over Borel E with μ(E) > 0) equal to min{1, h/χ}. Here h = inf_{n≥1} H(G_n)/n is the base-2 entropy of the law of the n-fold composed affine map, and χ = −Σ p_i log₂|r_i|. This matches Theorem 1.1. The only caveat is that the entropy rate is encoded as an infimum rather than a limit; Fekete's lemma makes these equal because H(G_n) is subadditive.

glossary.plain: Finite indexed family of maps x ↦ r_i x + t_i with 0<|r_i|<1, together with a strictly positive probability vector p.
glossary.standard_concept: Weighted self-similar IFS on ℝ (repeated generators allowed)

glossary.plain: Slope and offset of the composition φ_{i1}∘…∘φ_{in}, encoded as the pair (slope, offset).
P(G_n = g), where G_n is the random composed map of an i.i.d. p-word of length n.
glossary.standard_concept: Law of the random walk G_n on the affine group
glossary.note: Composition order does not affect the law, since i.i.d. words reversed have the same law.

glossary.plain: H(G_n) in bits, i.e. −Σ_g q_g log q_g / log 2.

glossary.standard_concept: Random-walk entropy rate h_RW = lim H(G_n)/n
glossary.note: Equal to the limit by subadditivity (Fekete). The set is nonempty and bounded below by 0.
Strictly positive under the structure hypotheses.
Together with IsProbabilityMeasure, this pins down Hutchinson's unique invariant measure.

glossary.standard_concept: Lower Hausdorff dimension of a measure
glossary.note: The paper notes that the conventions agree by exact dimensionality.

lean_claims.plain: Hypotheses: ι is a nonempty finite type, S is a System on ι, and μ is a Borel probability measure on ℝ with μ = Σ p_i (φ_i)_*μ. Conclusion: inf{dim_H E : E measurable, μ(E) > 0} = ofReal(min(1, (inf_{n≥1} H(G_n)/n) / χ)).

paper_claims.plain: For every finite nonempty family φ_i(x) = r_i x + t_i with 0 < |r_i| < 1 and every strictly positive probability vector p, the self-similar measure satisfies dim_H μ = min{1, h_RW/χ}. No separation is assumed; exact overlaps and repeated generators are allowed.

coverage.why: All hypotheses and definitions match. The entropy rate is taken as an infimum, which equals the limit by Fekete. The lower-dimension convention matches one of the conventions the paper says are equivalent.

flags.explanation: h_RW is encoded as inf_n H(G_n)/n rather than the limit. These are equal because H(G_{n+m}) ≤ H(G_n) + H(G_m), so this is a faithful encoding but not literally the paper's definition.

The Lean statement uses the lower Hausdorff dimension (inf over positive-measure sets). The paper states that, by exact dimensionality, either convention gives the same result, so this choice is acceptable.

lint_verdicts.why: Real.log 2 > 0, so the division is genuine.
negMulLog is continuous with 0·log 0 = 0, matching the standard entropy convention; masses lie in (0,1].
The range is nonempty and bounded below by 0, since entropies are nonnegative, so sInf is the true infimum.
|r_i| ∈ (0,1) by structure fields, so log is genuine and negative.
ofReal of positive weights is exact; affine maps are measurable, so map is genuine.
E = univ has μ(univ) = 1 > 0, so the infimum is over a nonempty family.
dim_H takes values in ℝ≥0∞ but is ≤ 1 on ℝ; the comparison with ofReal is fine.
The Lyapunov exponent is strictly positive under the structure hypotheses.
The argument of ofReal is ≥ 0 because h ≥ 0 and χ > 0, so no truncation occurs.
